Hardeep Punjab - A Treat for Tandoori Lovers!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Visited Hardeep Punjab recently and was truly impressed by the flavors and the variety! We ordered the Non-Veg Platter, and it was a feast of smoky, juicy, and perfectly marinated delights. The platter included creamy chicken tikka, spicy seekh kebabs, prawns, and fish, each one cooked to perfection. The chutneys and pickled onions served alongside added that extra punch.

The menu offers a wide range of non-veg appetizers – from Chaska Maska Tikka to Thai Tikka – and everything sounded tempting. The place has a nostalgic charm with its classic Punjabi touch, established since 1988, and it's clear why it’s a favorite in the area.

Service was quick, portions were generous, and the taste was genuinely authentic. Whether you're with friends or family, this is a solid place to enjoy rich Punjabi flavors.

Must-try: Non-Veg Platter, Prawns Lasooni Tikka, and Chicken Lollipop

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.name: Alok Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a seafood lover looking for authentic Mangalorean-style delicacies in Mumbai, Sion Lunch Home is the place to be. Located just a five-minute walk from Sion railway station, this eatery has been my go-to spot for the past two years, and I can confidently say it never disappoints.

Ambience & Seating

The place is clean and well-maintained, but it doesn’t have a very large seating capacity. Whether you opt for the AC or non-AC section, expect a waiting time—sometimes as long as 40 minutes to an hour. Due to its immense popularity, the restaurant does not accept reservations, so it’s always bustling with seafood enthusiasts.

Food & Specialties

The main reason for the crowd? The exceptional seafood, prepared in true Mangalorean style. I highly recommend trying their fish thalis and fish fries, which are consistently fresh and flavorful.

Must-Try Dishes:

Prawns Fry – Crispy, well-spiced, and utterly delicious.

Squid Fry – Perfectly cooked and packed with coastal flavors.

Bombil Fry – A Mumbai favorite that’s crispy on the outside, soft inside.

Pomfret Thali – A full-fledged meal featuring succulent pomfret fish.

Surmai Thali – A classic favorite for those who love kingfish.

Neer Dosa – Light, fluffy and an excellent companion to their flavorful gravies.

Mutton Sukka – My personal favorite; the spice blend is simply spot-on.

Fish Platters: A Family Favorite

If you’re visiting with family, the fish platters are a must-try. They offer a great variety and are perfect for sharing, ensuring you get to taste a bit of everything.

Final Verdict

Despite the long waiting time, the experience at Sion Lunch Home is always worth it. The food quality, authentic preparation, and reasonable prices make it one of the best places in Mumbai for seafood lovers. If you enjoy coastal cuisine, this spot should be at the top of your list!

featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vaidya
featured_reviews.review_text: Gurukripa is a great spot in Sion offering a wide variety of snacks and sweets at affordable prices (around ₹200–₹300 per person). While everything is decent, their samosa truly stands out crispy, flavorful, and absolutely worth trying. It’s no surprise that Gurukripa is well-known for its samosas, which are widely supplied to cinemas and theatres across the city. Definitely recommended for a quick and tasty bite!

featured_reviews.name: Desii Thing
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would have easily given 5 stars, but recently the overall taste seems to have gone slightly down compared to what it used to be.

Still, the samosa with chutney and chole remains their signature and is absolutely worth trying — crisp, flavourful, and perfectly balanced. The gulab jamun is also soft, rich, and makes a great finish to the meal.

They have a wide variety of chaats, North Indian snacks, sweets, and quick bites — most items are decent in quality and value for money. Service is fast, and this place continues to be a popular local landmark with a loyal fan following over the years.

Only minor downsides are the slightly toned-down spice and taste recently, limited seating comfort, and parking challenges due to the busy area.

Overall, still one of the must-try classic spots in Mumbai for samosa-chole lovers — just wish they bring back their old flavour punch!

featured_reviews.review_text:

We indulged in their Tisrya Thali, Prawns Thali, and Bombil Fry, each dish showcasing the rich flavors of coastal Malvan. The freshness of the seafood truly transported us to the shores of Malvan with every bite

For dessert, we had the delightful choice between Kharwas and caramel custard, and we opted for the Kharwas, which was a perfect end to our meal.

The manager's warmth and the impeccable service added to the overall experience, making our visit truly memorable. Masoli Lunch Home is undoubtedly a must-visit destination for anyone craving authentic Malvani flavors and exceptional hospitality

Overall 5/5

I’m really disappointed with my recent visit to Hanuman Veg. During my visit, I personally noticed what looked like poor hygiene practices, including bees and bugs hovering around the lemon and onion counter, which made me very uncomfortable about the cleanliness of the place.

The overall environment didn’t feel hygienic, and based on what I experienced, I no longer feel confident eating here. I genuinely hope the restaurant improves its standards, but for now, I personally wouldn’t recommend it, especially to anyone concerned about food safety.

featured_reviews.name: sonalee borse
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today I Ordered Veg Pulao and got it within 5 minutes — clearly preheated or just mixed everything on flame and served immediately. The rice was plain, flavourless, and cold after just one bite. When I mentioned it to the waiter, he said, “Madam, fan chal raha hai to thanda to ho gaya na.” Really disappointing response!
A simple apology or reheating would’ve fixed it, but instead, I was left with cold food and colder service. Definitely not worth the price or experience.

featured_reviews.name: Prem Chandra KR
featured_reviews.review_text:
A vegetarian restaurant at Sion circle.

Small in size. Less number of chairs and tables for dining. Moderately clean.

Service is lacking. The attendants at the table were busy chatting among themselves.

I had Curd rice. The taste was good. Quite expensive. Feels like it is not worth the money being spent. I have uploaded the menu card.

featured_reviews.name: TRAVEL CLEVER
featured_reviews.review_text:
Well this small little joint has surprised me with its delicious food and prompt service.

The restaurant is clean and maintained. I had breakfast at Hanuman. I had Mysore Masala Dosa, Misal Pav and tea.

The food was served piping hot. The Misal Pav was just perfectly served with onions and Pav. The food was quickly served.

I liked the Sambhar and chutney served with the dosa. The dosa was perfect crisp and the Masala in it was tasty too.

Overall enjoyed having a quick breakfast here.
